reading: Night staffing, repositioning and early detection form one causal chain: when a ward is short, repositioning slips (c1), and injuries that start as category 1 are missed, more often in darker skin (c4), until they are found at category 2. A protected round targets the middle of the chain (c2); the float nurse targets its start. Measurement sits outside the chain but can distort it, because incident reports undercount and rise with attention (c3). The multicentre ratio study quoted to the board remains an unverified lead.
